text: In ℤ[√−5] one has 6 = 2 · 3 = (1 + √−5)(1 − √−5). What does this show?
choices: ℤ[√−5] is not a UFD: 6 has two essentially different factorizations into irreducibles
2 is prime but not irreducible in ℤ[√−5]
explanation: All four factors are irreducible (norm arguments) and 2 is not an associate of 1 ± √−5, so factorization into irreducibles is not unique. Equivalently 2 is irreducible but NOT prime: it divides the product (1+√−5)(1−√−5) = 6 without dividing either factor.
